title: Salvage Rights
summary: The season's first wall ate a Guild crawler out on the pan — and a Reclaimer crew was winching it before the sand settled. Two claims, one wreck, decades of bad manners. By Driftline custom a neutral courier carries both claim tokens to the dockmaster at Keel Town, and the order they cross her desk decides who owns a fortune in stranded steel.

objectives.label: Take the Union's claim ingot from Pyke's office
Take the Guild's counter-claim, sealed in manifest wax, from Tamsin
Run both claims up to the winch base
Lay both claims on the dockmaster's desk — order matters

offer.text: Chief! Perfect, a neutral party with a fast bike and no lawyers. Storm dropped a Guild crawler on the pan two nights back. My crew had lines on it before the engines cooled — standard salvage, clearly posted, one hundred percent union-labeller legal.
Then the Guild arrives with a form that says a crawler 'in distress' is still their property, and suddenly MY winch crew is 'an armed infestation'. We are, at worst, a *polite* infestation.

Tamsin Cho, Guild band, since everyone is naming themselves. Courier: the custom is old and both sides honour it. One courier carries both claims to Keel Town. The dockmaster countersigns in the order received. First signature wins the wreck.
So the entire dispute comes down to which piece of metal I hand over first. This is the most honest politics I've ever heard of.

accept.text: Claim ingot's stamped and weighed, chief. Article Three: *we were there first, with tools*. Remember — the Guild wants that crawler shelved next to their conscience. We want it working. One of those is a *life*.

The Guild's counter-claim is in manifest wax. Do not read it, do not hum near it, and do not believe the bit where it calls the Reclaimers 'weather-adjacent'. …Personally, courier, I price arguments, not winners. But do ride *fast*.
Ketch here. Word of advice from the last courier who ran double claims — me, thirty years ago. Both tokens ride in separate panniers. Metal remembers what it's touching, and the desert loves a bribe.

complete.text: Both claims received, weighed, and warm from the road. Pen's ready, courier. Before I sign anything — log note for the record: I ran a crawler like her for six seasons. Whatever I sign, *somebody's* going to remember this order at every mooring from here to the gate. So choose like the desert's watching. It is.
Signed and witnessed, kid. However it fell — that's the job. The Driftline doesn't pick sides; it picks *up*. Both, mostly, at once.
Ogo on the Guild band. The Brinemaster has noted the courier's conduct in the crawler matter. Noted it *down*, with a date and a small star. The meaning of the star is Guild business.

choices.prompt: Dockmaster Shore holds the pen over the manifest. Which claim crosses her desk first?

options.text: The Guild's counter-claim. Property is property — the crawler was theirs before the storm.
The Union's claim ingot. They were there first, with tools — salvage is a kind of rescue.
